```tsx
  /* #3084 P34 — a "How to fix" link opens #/models?endpoint=<id>&field=<field>: open that editor
     once the endpoint is loaded and focus the field. Each link is handled once, so a later
     settings refresh never reopens the editor over the user's edits. */
  const stage = useAppSelector((s) => s.ui.stage);
  const focusEndpointId = stage.kind === 'model-manager' ? stage.endpointId : undefined;
  const focusField = stage.kind === 'model-manager' ? stage.endpointField : undefined;
  const handledFocus = useRef('');
  const [pendingFocus, setPendingFocus] = useState<string | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    const key = focusEndpointId ? `${focusEndpointId}|${focusField ?? ''}` : '';
    if (!key || handledFocus.current === key) return;
    const endpoint = endpoints.find((e) => e.id === focusEndpointId);
    if (!endpoint) return;
    handledFocus.current = key;
    open(endpoint);
    setPendingFocus(focusField && focusField in ENDPOINT_FIELD_TEST_IDS ? ENDPOINT_FIELD_TEST_IDS[focusField as keyof typeof ENDPOINT_FIELD_TEST_IDS] : null);
  }, [focusEndpointId, focusField, endpoints]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!pendingFocus || editing === undefined) return;
    const el = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-testid="${pendingFocus}"]`);
    el?.scrollIntoView?.({ block: 'center' });
    el?.focus();
    setPendingFocus(null);
  }, [pendingFocus, editing]);
```

```ts
/* #3084 W3d — OpenAI-compatible analyzer endpoints in mock mode (VITE_USE_MOCKS=true).
   Endpoint CRUD, keys, the catalog and the Test action are fulfilled in-process by the
   mock api layer; seeds arrive through window globals (see mockGetAnalyzerModels). */
import { test, expect, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import { waitForRouteReady, stubAccountModelProbes } from './helpers';

test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' });

test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  await stubAccountModelProbes(page);
});

async function addEndpoint(page: Page, opts: { name: string; baseUrl: string; context: string; gpu?: string; key?: string }) {
  await page.getByTestId('add-endpoint').click();
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-name').fill(opts.name);
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-base-url').fill(opts.baseUrl);
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-context-tokens').fill(opts.context);
  if (opts.gpu) await page.getByTestId('endpoint-gpu').selectOption(opts.gpu);
  if (opts.key) await page.getByTestId('endpoint-key').fill(opts.key);
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-save').click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('endpoint-editor')).toBeHidden();
}

test('add an endpoint (context required), pick its model, and the label shows "schema (not enforced)" from a Test record', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const w = window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
    w.__SEED_ENDPOINT_MODELS__ = { 'lab-server': ['qwen3-30b'] };
    w.__SEED_ANALYZER_CAPABILITIES__ = {
      'openai:lab-server::qwen3-30b': {
        serverUrl: 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1',
        testedAt: '2026-09-11T10:00:00.000Z',
        control: { ok: true },
        structuredOutput: { schema: { 'model-default': 'ignored' } },
        reasoning: {},
      },
    };
  });
  await page.goto('/#/models');
  await waitForRouteReady(page);

  await page.getByTestId('add-endpoint').click();
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-name').fill('Lab server');
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-base-url').fill('http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1');
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-save').click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('endpoint-context-error')).toBeVisible();
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-context-tokens').fill('32768');
  await page.getByTestId('endpoint-save').click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('endpoint-row-lab-server')).toBeVisible();

  const picker = page.getByTestId('account-default-analysis-model');
  await expect(picker.locator('option[value="openai:lab-server::qwen3-30b"]')).toHaveCount(1);
  await picker.selectOption('openai:lab-server::qwen3-30b');
  const label = page.getByTestId('analyzer-default-model-label');
  await expect(label).toContainText('Lab server · qwen3-30b');
  await expect(label).toContainText('schema (not enforced)');
  // Wave 5 appends "+ custom params" through runLabelSuffixes; asserted there, not here.
});

  await page.addInitScript(() => {

      { archiveId: null, kind: 'key', endpointId: 'lab', origin: 'http://10.0.0.5:8080', issues: ['analyzerEndpointKeys.lab.key: invalid_type'], droppedAt: '2026-09-13T10:00:00.000Z' },
```

```ts
  /* #3084 P31 e2e — a one-shot seed of dropped endpoint entries, consumed on the first settings
     read so the mock acknowledge route (3b Task 3b.6b) can remove them. This task relies on 3b's
     `mockAcknowledgeDroppedEndpointEntries`, which filters MOCK_USER_SETTINGS.droppedEndpointEntries
     by archive id and returns the settings body (w3ab Task 3b.6b, pinned by "mock
     acknowledgeDroppedEndpointEntries removes only the named entries"). This task's expectations
     match it: acknowledging 'a1' removes only that entry, and a `null`-archiveId entry is never
     named, so it stays listed. */
  const seededDrops = (globalThis as { __SEED_DROPPED_ENDPOINT_ENTRIES__?: UserSettings['droppedEndpointEntries'] }).__SEED_DROPPED_ENDPOINT_ENTRIES__;
  if (seededDrops) {
    MOCK_USER_SETTINGS.droppedEndpointEntries = seededDrops;
    delete (globalThis as { __SEED_DROPPED_ENDPOINT_ENTRIES__?: unknown }).__SEED_DROPPED_ENDPOINT_ENTRIES__;
  }
```

```ts
  it('every fix wikiPage names a wiki page that exists, with no anchor (#3084 P33)', () => {
    const fixes = [
      ...reasoningOverflowFixes({ transport: 'openai', model: 'qwen3-30b', endpointId: 'lab' }),
      ...reasoningOverflowFixes({ transport: 'gemini', model: 'gemini-3.5-flash' }),
      ...reasoningOverflowFixes({ transport: 'ollama', model: 'qwen3.5:4b' }),
    ];
    const openai = reasoningOverflowFixes({ transport: 'openai', model: 'qwen3-30b', endpointId: 'lab' });
    /* The settled fixes/reads rule, asserted by structure rather than position: actionable fixes first, then
       every `Read:` entry, and only a `Read:` entry links a page. A later wave can add a fix or a read and
       this stays green. */
    const firstRead = openai.findIndex((f) => f.label.startsWith('Read:'));
    expect(firstRead).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    expect(openai.slice(0, firstRead).every((f) => !f.label.startsWith('Read:') && f.wikiPage === undefined)).toBe(true);
    expect(openai.slice(firstRead).every((f) => f.label.startsWith('Read:') && typeof f.wikiPage === 'string')).toBe(true);
    expect(openai).toContainEqual({ label: 'Read: When a model thinks past its output limit', wikiPage: 'OpenAI-Compatible-Analyzer-Endpoints' });
    for (const fix of fixes.filter((f) => f.wikiPage)) {
      expect(fix.wikiPage, fix.label).toMatch(/^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$/);
      expect(existsSync(fileURLToPath(new URL(`../../../docs/wiki/${fix.wikiPage}.md`, import.meta.url))), fix.wikiPage).toBe(true);
    }
  });
```

````markdown
# OpenAI-Compatible Analyzer Endpoints

An **analyzer endpoint** is a server that speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions API: llama.cpp,
llama-swap, LM Studio, vLLM, LiteLLM or OpenRouter. Castwright can analyse a book on it instead
of the local Ollama daemon or the Gemini API.

Use an endpoint when:
- you already serve models with one of these tools and want Castwright to use them;
- the model you want is not in Ollama, or runs better on your server;
- the server is another machine on your network, or a paid gateway.

Keep local Ollama when you want Castwright to manage the model for you, and Gemini when you have no
GPU to spare. See [Analysis & the Analyzer](Analysis-and-the-Analyzer).

Add one in **Admin → Model Manager → Analyzer endpoints**. Its models then appear in every
analysis-model picker as `<endpoint name> · <model>`.

## The fields

| Field | What to enter |
|---|---|
| Name | Any label. The endpoint id is made from it (lowercase letters, digits and `-`, up to 40 characters) and never changes. |
| Base URL | The OpenAI-compatible root, usually ending in `/v1`. Each server's value is below. |
| API key | Optional. The key is bound to the base URL's **origin** (scheme, host and port) and is only sent there. Change the host or port and Castwright asks for the key again; tick "This server needs no key" if it has none. |
| Model | Picked from the list, and saved everywhere as `openai:<endpointId>::<model>`, for example `openai:lab::qwen3-30b`. If the list is empty, type the model id under the endpoint's row. |
| Context size | **Required.** The context the server actually serves per request, not the model's training context. **List models** fills it from served values (`max_model_len`, then `meta.n_ctx`, then `context_length`); **Detect** reads llama.cpp or llama-swap `/props`. |
| GPU card | `none` (a remote or CPU server), `any` (treated as sharing every card) or `cuda:N`. A `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1` base URL starts at `any`, anything else at `none`. Castwright uses it to ask before analysing on the card your voices use, and to unload this server when a voice model needs that card's memory. |
| Unload URL | Optional, same host and port as the base URL. Castwright sends it a POST to free the card for a voice model, once for each model that has served a request since Castwright started; `{model}` is replaced by that model. **Without `{model}` it unloads every model on that server**, including one that another card or app is using. |
| Concurrent requests | 1–16. Match the server's parallel slots. |
| Request ceiling | 1–240 minutes, default 30: the longest one request may run after it leaves the queue. |
| Structured output | `schema` sends Castwright's output schema; `json` asks for any JSON object; `off` sends neither. **Test** shows what a model really does. |
| Max output tokens | `0` is Auto: the server's listed output limit, or context minus input. |
| Max input tokens per request | Optional. When set, chunks are sized to fit it (see "Chunk size" below). |

## Servers

Every command and file below was checked against the tool's documentation on the date under it.
If your version is different, check its documentation before copying.

### llama.cpp (llama-server)

**Pick it when** you serve one GGUF model and want the fewest moving parts.

```bash
‹verify at implementation: llama-server launch command — model path, context size, parallel slots, host and port, API key›
```
_Checked against llama.cpp ‹verify at implementation: build› on ‹verify at implementation: date›._

- **Base URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:‹verify at implementation: default port›/v1`.
- **API key:** `--api-key <key>` or `LLAMA_API_KEY`. The server reads `Authorization` (with or without `Bearer `) or `X-Api-Key`; a wrong key answers 401. `/props` and `/v1/models` need the key; `/health` does not. <!-- planning facts §B6 -->
- **Context size:** the per-slot served context: `/props` → `default_generation_settings.n_ctx`, or `/v1/models` → `data[].meta.n_ctx`. Never `meta.n_ctx_train`, which is the training context. **Detect** with flavor llama.cpp reads it. <!-- §B2 -->
- **GPU card:** the card llama-server runs on, as `cuda:N`.
- **Unload URL:** ‹verify at implementation: whether llama-server exposes an unload endpoint; if not, write "none — llama-server serves one model"›.
- **Structured output:** `schema`, then run **Test**. Schema enforcement while a model is thinking cannot be assumed: ggml-org/llama.cpp#20345 was closed by a fix, and later reports say it recurs on Qwen3.6 and gpt-oss. <!-- §B5 -->
- **Pitfalls:**
  - A request waiting for a busy slot gets no reply headers until a slot frees. It counts against the request ceiling and fails as a timeout, not as unreachable. Set **Concurrent requests** to the server's slot count. <!-- §B1 -->
  - 401: the key is missing or wrong. Re-enter it on the endpoint.

### llama-swap

**Pick it when** several models share one or more cards and should load on demand.

```yaml
‹verify at implementation: a llama-swap config with one model — its cmd, capabilities.context and apiKeys›
```
_Checked against llama-swap ‹verify at implementation: version› on ‹verify at implementation: date›._

- **Base URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:‹verify at implementation: default port›/v1`.
- **API key:** `apiKeys` in the config. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, a Basic password or `x-api-key`. Inference, `/v1/models`, `/unload`, `/upstream/*` and `/api/*` need it; `/health` does not. <!-- §B9 -->
- **Context size:** llama-swap lists `context_length`, `context_window` and `meta.n_ctx` **only from your config's `capabilities.context`**, never from the running server. Set it there, or use **Detect** with flavor llama-swap and a model: that calls `GET /props?model=<id>`, which **loads the model**, so Castwright asks first. <!-- §B7, §B10 -->
- **GPU card:** the card the models run on. If models run on different cards, add one endpoint per card, each with its own models, or use `any`.
- **Unload URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/models/unload/{model}` unloads one model (200, or 404 if it is not loaded). `POST /api/models/unload` and `GET /unload` unload **every** model: do not use them on a shared server. Each call waits until the process stops, and needs the key when `apiKeys` is set. <!-- §B8 -->
- **Structured output:** as llama.cpp: `schema`, then **Test**.
- **Pitfalls:** List models shows no context when `capabilities.context` is not set; add it or Detect.

### LM Studio

**Pick it when** you manage models in the LM Studio app.

```bash
‹verify at implementation: starting LM Studio's server (app setting or lms CLI) and loading a model with a context length›
```
_Checked against LM Studio ‹verify at implementation: version› on ‹verify at implementation: date›._

- **Base URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:‹verify at implementation: default port›/v1`.
- **API key:** ‹verify at implementation: whether LM Studio's server takes a key; if not, leave it empty›.
- **Context size:** the loaded context, `/api/v1/models` → `loaded_instances[].config.context_length` (the model must be loaded). `/api/v0/models` → `max_context_length` is the model's maximum, not what is loaded. <!-- §B13 -->
- **GPU card:** the card LM Studio loads onto.
- **Unload URL:** ‹verify at implementation: an unload endpoint, or "none"›.
- **Structured output:** `schema` or `off`, **never `json`**: LM Studio answers `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}` with 400 `'response_format.type' must be 'json_schema' or 'text'` (reported through 0.4.21). <!-- §B13 -->

### vLLM

**Pick it when** you serve a model with high throughput on a Linux GPU box.

```bash
‹verify at implementation: vllm serve command with max model length and API key›
```
_Checked against vLLM ‹verify at implementation: version› on ‹verify at implementation: date›._

- **Base URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:‹verify at implementation: default port›/v1`.
- **API key:** ‹verify at implementation: the vLLM API key flag›.
- **Context size:** `/v1/models` → `max_model_len`, the served length. **List models** fills it. <!-- §B11 -->
- **GPU card:** the card(s) vLLM uses; `any` if it spans several.
- **Unload URL:** ‹verify at implementation: an unload endpoint, or "none"›.
- **Structured output:** `schema`, then **Test**.
- **Pitfalls:** a small `max_model_len` leaves little room for output; a 400 naming a token limit during **Test** is recorded as inconclusive, never as "rejected".

### LiteLLM

**Pick it when** one gateway fronts several providers or local servers.

```yaml
‹verify at implementation: a LiteLLM proxy config routing one model to a backend, with a master key›
```
_Checked against LiteLLM ‹verify at implementation: version› on ‹verify at implementation: date›._

- **Base URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:‹verify at implementation: default port›/v1`.
- **API key:** the proxy's key (‹verify at implementation: its config name›).
- **Context size:** your **backend's** served context. LiteLLM's `/v1/models` may list `max_input_tokens` / `max_output_tokens` from LiteLLM's own catalogue, not from the backend: do not copy those. <!-- §B14 -->
- **GPU card:** the backend's card if the backend runs on this machine, otherwise `none`.
- **Unload URL:** none: the unload URL must share the gateway's host and port.
- **Structured output:** depends on the backend; run **Test**.

### OpenRouter

**Pick it when** you want hosted models with no GPU of your own.

- **Base URL:** `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` (‹verify at implementation: against OpenRouter's documentation›).
- **API key:** your OpenRouter key, bound to `https://openrouter.ai`.
- **Context size:** `/api/v1/models` → `context_length`, and `top_provider.context_length`; **List models** fills it. <!-- §B12 -->
- **GPU card:** `none`. **Unload URL:** none.
- **Max output tokens:** `top_provider.max_completion_tokens` is the provider's limit. <!-- §B12 -->
- **Pitfalls:** an output cap larger than what is left of the context is a 400; **Test** records it as inconclusive, and a run shows which limit to lower.

## Fallback

- When this endpoint cannot be reached (connection refused, host not found, or no connection
  within the connect timeout), Castwright hands that call, one hop, to **Advanced Settings →
  Analyzer fallback**: `off`, `local` (the Ollama model a local run uses, shown in the setting), `gemini` (the default; needs a
  Gemini API key) or another endpoint model.
- A reply that breaks off mid-stream, a reset or a proxy's 502 is **retried**, never a fallback.
- The fallback is never itself wrapped. If it is unreachable too, the run fails naming both.
- The switch is always announced, for example
  `Analyzer endpoint unreachable (Lab · qwen3-30b) — switched to Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash-lite)`.
- Saving a fallback that names a missing endpoint, or `gemini` with no key, is refused. An endpoint
  the fallback names cannot be deleted until the fallback changes.
- An install that turned the old Model Manager "Cloud fallback" switch off reads as `off` until you
  choose a target.

## Chunk size

Castwright splits each chapter so a request fits the endpoint:

- each stage's chunks are at most **its input fraction × Context size × 2 characters per token**,
  capped by that pass's ceiling;
- **Max input tokens per request**, or the endpoint model's TPM limit in Advanced Settings →
  Analyzer rate limits (whichever is smaller), lowers that further.

The inputs are the endpoint's **Context size** and **Max input tokens per request**, and Advanced
Settings → Analyzer chunking (`analyzer.stage1.localInputFraction`,
`analyzer.stage2.localInputFraction`, `analyzer.stage1.chunkCharBudget`,
`analyzer.stage2.chunkCharBudget`). All of them can be changed at any time.

## When a model thinks past its output limit

**What you see:** the run stops with `analyzer-reasoning-overflow`. The model spent its whole output
budget thinking and gave no answer. Castwright starts no new model calls; chapters already running
finish and are kept.

**Fix:** the failure's "How to fix" links open these settings:

1. Raise the endpoint's **Max output tokens**, or set it to `0` (Auto). It cannot exceed what the
   server allows.
2. Check **Context size** matches what the server serves: more context leaves more room for output.
3. Lower the stage input fractions (Advanced Settings → Analyzer chunking), so each chunk leaves
   more room.

Then resume — finished chapters are kept.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| ‹verify at implementation: the analyzer-unreachable message for an endpoint› | Connection refused, host not found, or the connection timed out | Start the server; check the host and port. The fallback runs if one is set. |
| A 502, or "reset" in the server log | The server or a proxy failed mid-reply. Castwright retries it. | Check the server's own log. This never triggers the fallback. |
| ‹verify at implementation: the auth message for a key bound to another host› | The base URL's host or port changed after the key was saved | Re-enter the key on the endpoint. |
| A 400 naming a context, token or length limit | The output cap plus the input exceed what the server allows | Lower Max output tokens, or correct Context size. |
| `schema (partial)` beside the model | ‹verify at implementation: meaning, from structuredOutputLabel› | ‹verify at implementation› |
| `schema (not enforced)` beside the model | **Test** found the model ignores the schema | Use `json` or `off`, or a model that enforces the schema. |
| A banner: "Some analyzer endpoint settings were malformed and were removed" | An endpoint or key entry in `user-settings.json` failed validation when settings were read. It was removed so the rest load, and copied to `user-settings.invalid-endpoints.json` | Add the endpoint again, then **Got it**. |
````

```markdown
### ‹A-new-1› · Long silent prefill completes on an endpoint ([#3084](https://github.com/dudarenok-maker/Castwright/issues/3084), PR #NNNN) · **slower card of a 2-card box, llama-swap with a ≥64k-context model**

The OpenAI transport starts its idle watchdog only after the first delta and bounds the
call with the endpoint's request ceiling (default 30 min). Automated tests use a fake
server; only a real prefill of a very long prompt shows that no timeout, retry or
fallback fires before the first token.

- Add the llama-swap endpoint with `gpu` = the slower card, context ≥ 64k, and analyse a
  chapter whose stage-1 prompt exceeds 64k tokens.
- Observe the server log: no `analyzer-timeout`, no idle retry, no fallback announcement;
  the chapter completes. Record time to first token and total time.
- Criteria: `docs/testing/openai-analyzer-onbox-acceptance.md` § "Long silent prefill".

### ‹A-new-2› · Same-card eviction of an endpoint for a Qwen load ([#3084](https://github.com/dudarenok-maker/Castwright/issues/3084), PR #NNNN) · **2-card boot (8 GB + 16 GB), llama-swap with a per-model unload URL, Qwen TTS**

`withCapacityRetry` POSTs the unload URL of every idle endpoint on the denied card (or
`any`): once per model whose request was sent to the endpoint and not unloaded since, with
the endpoint's busy state (a run using it, or a call in flight) re-checked before every POST.
The endpoint lever has no latch: Ollama keeps its own once-per-call latch and gate, and the
endpoint lever is bounded instead by one POST per (endpoint, model) per admission, 10 s each
— a worst case of Σ (served models on matching endpoints) × 10 s. An admission is one
synthesize call, not one chapter. A 2xx or 404 removes the model from the served set. Unit
tests use fake servers; only real VRAM and a real run show that the card frees when idle and
is never unloaded under a live run.

- **Idle, one served model.** Endpoint `gpu` = `cuda:N` (the card Qwen targets), unload URL
  `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/models/unload/{model}`. One analysis call must have completed
  first, so the endpoint has a served model. With no analysis running, load Qwen on that
  card: the log shows one unload POST, capacity is re-probed, and Qwen loads without
  running out of memory.
- **Other card.** Pin Qwen to the other card: no unload POST.
- **Mid-run, between chunk calls.** Start an analysis on the endpoint. Watch the server log
  for a completed chunk call, then trigger a Qwen load on the endpoint's card **before the
  next chunk call starts** (no request in flight, run still active). Expect no unload POST:
  the Qwen load waits or fails with the capacity message. The next chunk call succeeds
  without a model reload (no llama-swap load line). Resume/Regenerate also prompts.
- **Two served models.** Run phase 0 and phase 1 on two different models of the same
  llama-swap endpoint, let the run finish, then load Qwen on the card: two unload POSTs,
  one per model, both models gone from `GET /running` (llama-swap). Unload Qwen and load it
  again without analysing: no unload POST this time (both models left the served set).
- **Two endpoints on one card, one busy.** Two llama-swap endpoints (two ports) on the same
  card, both with served models. Start an analysis on endpoint B only, then trigger a Qwen
  load: endpoint A is unloaded at once and B logs one "busy; not unloading" line. Let B's run
  finish while the admission is still polling: B is then unloaded within the same admission
  (its POST appears after A's, before the give-up). If the admission gives up first, the
  failure names B as "busy for the whole wait".
- **All-models URL.** Edit the unload URL to drop `{model}` (e.g. `/api/models/unload`):
  Settings shows the "unloads every model on that server" warning, and the save succeeds.
- **No URL.** Remove the unload URL and repeat the idle case: the failure message names
  "Unload URL".
- **A run that starts while the unload POST is out.** As the mid-run case, but time the Qwen
  load so the analyzer's next chunk call starts **while** the unload POST is still blocked on
  llama-swap stopping the model. Expect what an Ollama eviction does today: the chapter
  continues, the endpoint reloads the model on that call (one llama-swap load line), and TTS
  admission retries. Record both timestamps and whether the chapter failed. Also confirm the
  log holds ONE "busy; not unloading" line for that admission, not one per poll.
- **After a restart, with nothing run yet.** Restart Castwright while the endpoint still holds a
  model, and load Qwen on its card without analysing first: no unload POST is sent (Castwright
  has no model name for `{model}`), and the capacity failure names that endpoint and says no
  model has run on it since Castwright started.
- **A slow or unresponsive unload endpoint (found in review).** Point the unload URL at a
  server that never answers (or answers past 10 s), with two served models, then load Qwen on
  its card and let the admission poll several times before giving up. Expect exactly ONE
  unload POST per model for the whole admission — two, not one per poll — and the lever's
  share of the wait bounded near 2 × 10 s (Σ served models × 10 s), not `maxAttempts` × 10 s.
  The failure names the endpoint and says every unload request failed. Then queue a chapter
  render against the same card: each denied synthesize call repeats that cost (the models stay
  in the served set while the server is down) — record how many synth ops were denied and
  the total time lost, because this is the per-synth-op multiplication the unit bound hides.
- Criteria: `docs/testing/openai-analyzer-onbox-acceptance.md` § "Same-card eviction".

### ‹A-new-3› · Fallback to a smaller context leaves room to answer ([#3084](https://github.com/dudarenok-maker/Castwright/issues/3084), PR #NNNN) · **one GPU box: a llama.cpp `llama-server` endpoint with a ≥64k context, and Ollama with `analyzer.ollama.numCtx` ≤ 16k**

After a fallback switch, chunks sized for the primary's larger context reach a smaller one. The
pre-send guard (Task 3d.4b) measures each body against the target pass's budget, so every prompt
it lets through should leave the target room for the instructions and the answer. The automated
tests use fake analyzers. Only real servers show what happens when prompt plus output approach
the context: a context shift, an early stop, or an error.

- **Endpoint → Ollama.** Primary: the llama.cpp endpoint (context ≥ 64k), `analyzer.fallback.target`
  = `local`, Ollama `num_ctx` ≤ 16k. Analyse a long chapter and stop `llama-server` during
  phase 0. After the switch announcement, record for every chunk the target receives the
  `prompt_eval_count` and `eval_count` Ollama reports against `num_ctx`, and its `done_reason`.
  Expect `prompt_eval_count + eval_count` under `num_ctx` on every chunk, no `done_reason: length`,
  and no truncated JSON.
- **Ollama → llama.cpp.** Swap the roles: Ollama as the primary with a large `num_ctx`, and the
  llama.cpp endpoint started with a small context (`-c 16384`) as the target. Stop Ollama mid-run.
  For each request record `timings.prompt_n` and `timings.predicted_n` from the response, and any
  context-shift line or "exceeds the available context size" error in the `llama-server` log.

- **Refused, not sent.** Lower the target's context until a chunk cannot be split further, and run
  annotate-emotion over a chapter sized for the primary: the chapter fails with the input-too-large
  copy (or, for an escalation window, the skip warning is logged), and the target's own log shows
  no request for it.
- Criteria: `docs/testing/openai-analyzer-onbox-acceptance.md` § "Fallback to a smaller context".
```

Each (endpoint, model) gets at most one POST per admission, 10&nbsp;s each: a worst case of Σ served models × 10&nbsp;s, repaid per denied synthesize call, not per chapter. `docs/release-notes-next.md`:

```markdown
- **OpenAI-compatible analyzer endpoints are selectable** (#3084, W3d). Model Manager → Analyzer endpoints adds, edits and deletes named servers (llama.cpp / llama-swap, LM Studio, vLLM, LiteLLM, OpenRouter) with a required served context size (List models prefill from `max_model_len` / `meta.n_ctx` / `context_length`; on-demand Detect with a "may load the model" confirmation for llama-swap), an origin-bound API key that must be re-entered when the host changes, a GPU card (`none` / `any` / `cuda:N`, loopback hosts default to `any`), an optional same-origin unload URL with `{model}` substitution (one POST per model that has served the endpoint; a URL without `{model}` saves with an all-models warning), concurrency, request ceiling and structured-output mode. `selectAnalyzer` builds `OpenAIAnalyzer`. A new Advanced Settings knob, `analyzer.fallback.target` (`ANALYZER_FALLBACK_TARGET`, the first `analyzer-engine` knob type, default `gemini`; `off` / `local` / `gemini` / an endpoint model), replaces the `allowCloudFallback` rule for Ollama and endpoint primaries: one hop, only on unreachable; the target's own key-origin and capability checks run on its first call; a GPU-bound target carries the run's busy marks; the switch announcement and a both-unreachable failure name both; a missing endpoint or a keyless `gemini` is refused at save; `findEndpointReferences` counts it; a saved `allowCloudFallback: false` reads as `off` with no migration; Model Manager's Cloud fallback row is gone. **The default fallback for anyone who adds an endpoint is Gemini** (when a Gemini key is set): an unreachable endpoint's calls go to Gemini unless the target is switched off or retargeted in Advanced Settings → Analyzer fallback, which shows the effective target (a legacy `off` with its reason, `local` with its concrete model and a not-installed warning, and a keyless `gemini` as inactive). **After a fallback to a smaller-context model, an oversized request is split, or clearly failed with `AnalyzerTargetInputTooLargeError` ("prompt is larger than the fallback target … can take (context N tokens)", coded `analyzer-request-rejected` with fixes for the fallback target and the stage input fractions), instead of being silently truncated on input; the non-story check logs such a skip.** **A fallback target holds GPU busy marks only once it activates**, never from run start, so a healthy run does not block TTS eviction of a same-card fallback endpoint; from the switch on, the job's chunk budgets and phase events follow the target. A local primary never falls back to `local`. `analysisEngine` accepts `openai`, and a saved `openai` engine whose default model is not an endpoint id fails before the run with `analyzer-endpoint-missing`. An endpoint is busy while a call to it is in flight or an analysis/script-review run using it is active; TTS capacity admission unloads idle endpoints on the denied card, re-checking each endpoint's busy state before every unload POST and logging one "busy; not unloading" line per endpoint per admission (Ollama's lever is untouched and keeps its own gate and latch; the endpoint lever has no latch and is reached only on an iteration where Ollama was not evicted, so a 2xx unload retries admission and the next denial re-measures free memory before either lever runs again; it is bounded by one unload POST per (endpoint, model) per admission at 10 s each — Σ served models × 10 s at worst, and an admission is one synthesize call, not one chapter — so an endpoint that goes idle mid-wait is still unloaded and a slow or hanging unload server is not re-POSTed on every poll; a model counts as unloadable once a request has been sent to it, Tests included, and leaves that set once an unload answers 2xx or 404; the failure message names every sharing endpoint still holding the card and why — no Unload URL, busy for the whole wait, every unload request failed, unloaded what it could and still short, or no model run on it since Castwright started). `Layout` now loads the config on mount and feeds the guards the device the sidecar reports for an `auto` TTS engine (a resident Qwen's own card, or CPU for an engine the sidecar runs on CPU), so the forward/reverse GPU guards and the generation hold know the TTS card in every session; they compare every live generation's card with the endpoint's and fail closed only when neither the knob nor the sidecar names one. Pickers list endpoint models and run labels show the structured-output mode. Endpoint saves show each refusal's `issues[]` next to its field; entries dropped from settings at read show a banner in Model Manager and Advanced Settings with "Got it" (entries whose archive copy is still pending say so and cannot be dismissed); an endpoint overflow fix opens that endpoint's editor at the field (`#/models?endpoint=<id>&field=<field>`). New wiki page `OpenAI-Compatible-Analyzer-Endpoints` (setup per server, fallback, chunk size, overflow, troubleshooting).
```

`RELEASE_NOTES.md`:

```markdown
- **Analyse with your own OpenAI-compatible server.** Point Castwright at llama.cpp, llama-swap, LM Studio, vLLM or OpenRouter, tell it which graphics card the server uses, and pick its models anywhere you choose an analysis model. Castwright asks before analysing on the card your voices are using, frees that card when a voice model needs it, and shows whether the model really follows its output format. If a server can't be reached, analysis falls back to Gemini by default (when you have a Gemini key); switch that off, or send it to your local model or another server, in Advanced Settings. A fallback only claims its graphics card once it actually takes over, and if it falls back to a smaller model, oversized requests are split or clearly fail rather than being cut short. And if a saved server setting was damaged, Castwright tells you what it removed. A new wiki page walks through setting up each server.
```
